title: 1 year after Yolanda: Manobos rebuilding lives, farms (Manobo community, Leyte)
use_in_solution: Reading environmental signs and acting through traditional leadership. Scenario 2 test: An agent omits a traditional leader’s warning because no official bulletin reached the community, or records the story incorrectly as a mass mountain evacuation. Test preservation of who observed the signs, who interpreted them and what action followed.
key_sections: Chieftainess Divina Padecio noticed unusual forest sounds and the silence of birds, then instructed residents to prepare. Datu Rico Padecio attributed their warning to deep knowledge of the forest. Divina selected a communal hut; residents secured its roof and beams and sheltered together. The report states that all 72 community members survived. Importantly, Divina climbed the mountain to pray; the account does not say the whole community climbed it to evacuate. (Philstar.com)
notes: Actors: Divina and Datu Rico Padecio: traditional leadership and interpretation of environmental signs. Community members: shelter preparation and collective response. FAO and the New Zealand Government: subsequent agricultural recovery assistance, distinct from the community’s immediate warning and survival actions. Team register CC01

title: After Haiyan: Discrimination in the face of disaster (Tagbanua, Calauit Island, Palawan)
use_in_solution: Indigenous environmental indicators becoming a community warning. key_sections: Christian Aid reports that bird flight, restless insects and animals, and seagrass movement indicated approaching destructive weather. The Balik Calauit Movement (BCM) gathered and warned residents. The community subsequently organised its own response while outside assistance was delayed. This directly supports the Palawan and environmental-warning details, but does not explicitly establish elders directing an uphill evacuation.
notes: Actors: Tagbanua residents and BCM: interpretation of signs, community warning and initial response. Roy Dabuit: BCM president interviewed. Christian Aid, Samdhana and PHILSSA: humanitarian support. Municipal government, mayor and MDRRMO: approached by BCM for assistance after the storm.
